what: RUN 1 (log lines 1 to 1222) IS SUPERSEDED, kept as a false start. Two modelling defects of mine, found by reading its verdicts: (1) the bench's pool was tied to the opponent's pool (DJ = NA) or to the chooser's (DJ = N + L in C1), so 'at 12D' meant a 12D bench as well and contempt at 12D was near-certain by construction; (2) relationship goods (names given to an inquisitor, enemies made, a patron implicated) were scored at 0.05 to 0.15 and weighted at most 0.05, i.e. worth under a hundredth of a sentence, which made grace confession and impugning motive nearly free. Run 2 fixes the bench at 5D (the chooser's pool alone varies), puts relationship goods in their own units (1 per person or cluster) with their own weight ranges, adds the inquisitorial cluster rule (a conceded fact yields names), a scene cost for appearing, and the mortal-enemy rule; run 1's verdicts are not used by the proposal
